verdicts.title: Classifying the globally rigid edge-transitive graphs and distance-regular graphs in the plane
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: A graph is said to be globally rigid if almost all embeddings of the graph's vertices in the Euclidean plane will define a system of edge-length equations with a unique (up to isometry) solution. verdicts.title: A graph-state based synthesis framework for Clifford isometries
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We tackle the problem of Clifford isometry compilation, i.e, how to synthesize a Clifford isometry into an executable quantum circuit. We propose a simple framework for synthesis that only exploits the elementary properties of the Clifford group and one equation of the symplectic group. We highlight the versatility of our framework by showing that several normal forms of the literature are natural corollaries.
